where: section 2 and worked example 1 (also the figure note)
problem: The chosen design value RC = 10 µs is not a good choice for fc = 100 kHz, because the carrier period is T = 1/fc = 10 µs. With RC = T the capacitor falls to e^(−1) ≈ 0.37 of the peak between carrier peaks, so the ripple is about 63 % of the peak — the output plainly does not 'hold the peak' as the figure claims. The lower limit 1/(2π fc) = 1.59 µs is only a filter-cutoff limit; the ripple limit a designer actually needs is RC ≫ 1/fc = 10 µs.
fix: Keep the stated bounds 1/(2π fc) ≪ RC ≪ 1/(2π W) = 1.59 µs ≪ RC ≪ 159.15 µs, but choose a value well above the carrier period, for example RC = 100 µs (droop between peaks e^(−10/100) ≈ 0.90, about 10 % ripple, and still below 159 µs so no diagonal clipping at m = 0.5). Say that the ripple condition is RC ≫ 1/fc and use 100 µs in the example, the dry-run table and the figure note.

where: worked example 1 step 4 and quiz Q7
problem: Powers of ten are typed as plain digits: '1.59 × 10−6 s', '1/(2π × 106)', '1.59 × 10−7 s'. A student can read 106 as one hundred six and 10−7 as 'ten minus seven'.
fix: Use the superscript tag: 1.59 × 10<sup>−6</sup> s, 1/(2π × 10<sup>6</sup>), 1.59 × 10<sup>−7</sup> s.
